# User stories

MechaHarness acceptance paths are told as **user stories**: short scenes about what a product needs to do, written for readers who understand features but not code. Each story has a human **narrative**, an **implementation** section that traces library code fulfilling the feature, and a **validation** section that describes how the story is tested. Related stories are grouped into **suites** (`suite.yaml` + `stages/*.yaml`) with shared vars/setup and `parallel` or `sequential` execution. Stage order is lexicographic stage filenames (`010_…`, `020_…`). Story and suite text live only in fixtures under `tests/fixtures/models/`. This guide is **generated** from those fixtures.

See the Cursor skill `.cursor/skills/user-stories/SKILL.md` when adding features: edit stage YAML, regenerate this page, and keep twin copies of the same story id identical.

## Personas

### Nubble — operations / DevOps

Nubble keeps production and CI reliable. He cares about the right inference profile being loaded, cost and progress signals he can forward to billing or monitoring, and metrics that explain whether parallel work actually helped.

### Fangore — application developer

Fangore builds product applications on MechaHarness. He cares about deny-by-default permissions, product rules that models cannot override, durable local plans that survive crashes, loops that stop when they are not making progress, and context that never silently drops mandatory requirements.

### Taloneth — ML engineer

Taloneth owns judge contracts, adapter drift checks, and harness experiments. He cares about offline fixture batches, versioned recorded replies, honest shadow comparisons, validator qualification before promotion, research that rejects failing candidates, and decision exports that do not leak future outcomes.

## Running the suite

Default CI runs **every** story offline (static fixture + cassettes) — no skips. `./run_checks.sh` runs unit pytest without the story suite modules, then runs those suites once under `scripts/story_coverage.py` (so stages are not paid for twice).

```bash
# CI / offline — all stories, zero skips
pytest -q tests/stories

# Full suite (unit + stories)
pytest -q

# Live — every model-using story against real reason + judge hosts
# (HTTP twins + static infer/judge walks; softens cassette-exact token counts)
MECHA_STORY_BACKEND=live   MECHA_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1   MECHA_MODEL=qwen3-30b-thinking   MECHA_JUDGE_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8009   MECHA_JUDGE_MODEL=laya   MECHA_MAX_TOKENS=1024   pytest -q tests/stories

# Live OpenAI-compat only
MECHA_STORY_BACKEND=live MECHA_STORY_MODEL=openai_compat/qwen3-30b-thinking \
  MECHA_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1 pytest -q tests/stories -k nubble_run_cost

# Live System One only
MECHA_STORY_BACKEND=live MECHA_STORY_MODEL=systemone/laya \
  MECHA_JUDGE_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8009 pytest -q tests/stories -k refund_verdict

# Shorthand aliases (still dual-mode stories, not separate skipif modules)
MECHA_LIVE_OPENAI_COMPAT=1 MECHA_BASE_URL=… pytest -q tests/stories -k nubble_run_cost
MECHA_LIVE_QWEN=1 MECHA_BASE_URL=… pytest -q tests/stories -k nubble_run_cost
MECHA_LIVE_JUDGE=1 pytest -q tests/stories -k 'refund_verdict or systemone_cassette'
```

| `MECHA_STORY_BACKEND` | Behavior |
|-----------------------|----------|
| `static` (default) | In-process fixture + HTTP cassettes |
| `live` | Real servers; behavioral expects hard, cassette-exact token counts soft |

Live collects HTTP cassette twins **and** static stories that call `infer` / `judge` / `judge_route` (not pure policy, recipe-shape, `tool_loop`, or Anthropic-only walks). Flip `MECHA_STORY_BACKEND=live` with reason + judge URLs to prove cassettes are not fantasy.

## Models

| Path | Role |
|------|------|
| `static/fixture/v1` | Generic in-process model; model-agnostic paths |
| `openai_compat/<served-id>/v1` | Captured OpenAI-compat chat |
| `systemone/<served-id>/v1` | Captured System One judge wire |

## Suites

Suites live under `static/fixture/v1/suites/<suite_id>/`. Authored meta is `suite.yaml` (title, persona, execution mode, workspace, setup). Stages are `stages/<nn>_<slug>.yaml` (prose + runnable walk in one file). Generated `suite.json` mirrors discovered stages for the harness. **Parallel** suites run stages as isolated cases (name order is for stable CI only). **Sequential** suites share a workspace and stop on the first failure; stage order is the lexicographic stage filename. Pytest: `test_user_story_suite`; HTTP twins still run via `test_user_story`.

**Sequential run ids:** each sequential suite run creates a durable id under `.mechaharness/suite_runs/<run_id>/` (workspace + `manifest.json` + `RUN_ID.txt`). The id is printed in a banner (`pytest -s`) and as a warning; `LATEST` / `<suite_id>.latest` point at it. Resume or rerun from a stage without redoing priors:

```bash
# Fresh sequential run (note the printed run_id)
pytest -s -q tests/stories/test_user_story_suites.py -k calc_cli

# Continue / rerun from a stage stem using the shared workspace
MECHA_SUITE_RUN_ID=$(cat .mechaharness/suite_runs/calc_cli.latest) \
  MECHA_SUITE_FROM=030_fangore_calc_mul_div \
  pytest -s -q tests/stories/test_user_story_suites.py -k calc_cli
```

`MECHA_SUITE_FROM` accepts `story/scenario`, a unique scenario stem, or a 0-based index. `MECHA_SUITE_RUNS_DIR` overrides the runs root.

Sequential **coding-delegate** arcs (shared workspace, live Completer, contract verify): `calc_cli` (single-file expression CLI), `counter_pkg` (package + pytest + CLI), and `delegate_pkg` (list-mode, thorough guidance, red-green, refactor). Live Completer is the gate before trusting static stubs. MCP reuses the same graph — see `docs/guides/coding-delegate-suites.md`.

After editing stage YAML or `suite.yaml` / `personas.json`:

```bash
python -m tests.stories.commands sync-suites
python -m tests.stories.commands sync-guide
python -m tests.stories.commands sync-suites --check
python -m tests.stories.commands sync-guide --check
```

## Nubble's stories

### `nubble_anthropic_cassette_infer` — Infer through the Anthropic strategy with a cassette

Nubble proves the Anthropic Messages backend is a first-class reason lane without a live model. He starts the CLI host with family pass-through and backend anthropic (cassette from response.json), uses the default one-shot infer universe, runs infer with a short prompt, and verifies completion by matching the cassette text plus inference/cost events and token totals from the recorded usage.

#### Implementation

`UserStoryScenario.environment.backend=anthropic` builds `AnthropicStrategy` + `MemoryAsyncHttpClient` against `response.json` (`/v1/messages`). `cli:infer` / `CliInferRunner` emits `core:inference` with usage and priced `core:cost`.

#### Validation

Harness `user_story` scenario `cassette_infer.yaml`: environment backend anthropic, infer step, complete expects for event_types, text, tokens, cost_units.

### `nubble_ci_static_smoke` — Prove the HTTP adapter in CI without a live model host

The local inference host is offline, but a pull request still needs green CI. Nubble wants the OpenAI-compatible path proven from a cassette — a recorded reply replayed through the real HTTP client — so merges do not depend on LAN reachability.

#### Implementation

`OpenAICompatStrategy` implements Chat Completions HTTP for reason-lane backends. CLI universe `cli:infer` via `CliInstrumentor` / `CliInferRunner` runs that strategy so cassette replay exercises the real client path and the same EventLog baseline as other one-shot runs.

Covers: offline CI / OpenAI-compat smoke.

#### Validation

Harness `cli` scenario `cassette_smoke.yaml`: nonempty assistant text, positive cost units, exact baseline EventLog types. Cassette `response.json`. Live: `MECHA_STORY_BACKEND=live`.

#### Footnotes

1. [OpenAI Chat Completions](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/chat) — Wire models for reason-lane HTTP

### `nubble_graph_event_correlators` — Join every graph event to its graph, recipe, and authority

Nubble starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`. Nubble loads graph events into a warehouse and cannot afford to open checkpoints to learn which graph, recipe, or authorization epoch produced a row. A multi-node run with a nested subgraph must stamp every event with the same graph id, recipe stamp, and epoch, and nested runs must point at their parent run so a flat table can rebuild per-node attempts[^obs-analytics].

#### Implementation

Graph lifecycle emits carry warehouse correlators (`graph_id`, `recipe_id`, `authorization_epoch`, nest `parent_run_id` / `nest_depth`). `project_node_attempt_rows` projects attempt rows. `CliInstrumentor` verb `graph_event_correlators`.

Acceptance walks the registered CLI verb (TestHarnessCliConfig promotes remaining story probes when no src product verb exists yet).

#### Validation

Harness `user_story` walks the promoted product/test verb (no `probe:` wrapper); hard expects on declared observation keys.

#### Footnotes

[^obs-analytics]: [Event analytics schema (OBS-A01..A06)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/requirements/event-analytics-schema.md) — Correlator contract and fact/dimension decomposition

### `nubble_insp_coordination_cost` — Report parallel coordination cost on fan-out

Nubble starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`. Nubble compares wall-clock critical path, duplicated context, and fan-in review cost so parallelism is measured rather than assumed beneficial. Accepts WalkingLabs L14 and P08 guidance[^wl-l14-coord][^wl-p08-coord].

#### Implementation

`CoordinationCostMetrics` and `summarize_coordination_cost` in `mechaharness.coordination_cost` report fan-out orchestration cost, including graphs tiled from the `fan_out_aggregate` Agentic Recipe.

#### Validation

Harness `user_story` drives product verb(s) with environment `pass_through`/`mock`; hard expects on declared observation keys.

#### Footnotes

[^wl-l14-coord]: [WalkingLabs L14 Graph Engineering](https://walkinglabs.github.io/learn-harness-engineering/en/lectures/lecture-14-graph-engineering/) — Coordination cost
[^wl-p08-coord]: [WalkingLabs P08 First Explicit Graph](https://walkinglabs.github.io/learn-harness-engineering/en/projects/project-08-graph-engineering-first-graph/) — Measure parallelism

### `nubble_insp_efficiency_scorecard` — Keep multidimensional efficiency dimensions observable

Nubble starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`. Nubble needs tool calls, tokens, latency, and coordination cost kept as separate efficiency dimensions rather than a single opaque proxy. Accepts FineEnvs tool-call efficiency observations[^fineenvs-efficiency].

#### Implementation

`EfficiencyScorecard` and `build_efficiency_scorecard` in `mechaharness.efficiency_scorecard` compose topology/cost/coordination/resume dimensions without silent collapse.

#### Validation

Harness `user_story` drives product verb(s) with environment `pass_through`/`mock`; hard expects on declared observation keys.

#### Footnotes

[^fineenvs-efficiency]: [FineEnvs multi-harness RL — tool calls and tokens](https://fineenvs-multi-harness-rl.hf.space/?__theme=system#tool-calls-and-tokens) — MH-MHRL-19

### `nubble_insp_environment_delta` — Project environment context as versioned deltas

Nubble starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`. Nubble sends environment deltas instead of repeating full snapshots while still reconstructing deterministic state. Accepts WalkingLabs Codex guidance[^wl-codex-delta].

#### Implementation

`EnvironmentSnapshot`, `EnvironmentDelta`, `emit_delta`, and `apply_deltas` in `mechaharness.environment_delta`.

#### Validation

### `nubble_lane_load_hint` — Refuse work when the wrong inference profile is loaded

Nubble starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`. Nubble is on call when a refund-routing job fails on the local inference host. The job needs the judge profile, but an earlier experiment left the reason profile loaded instead. The harness must not fail with a vague error. It must tell him, in plain operator language, that this work needs the judge lane and which load command to run. When he switches to the correct profile, the page clears. He uses this story whenever a profile mismatch wastes incident time.

#### Implementation

Exclusive lanes (reason / decide-judge / media) on `InferenceEnvironment` refuse cross-lane work and surface load hints (`DEFAULT_LANE_LOAD_HINTS`). This is the operator-facing half of decide-versus-reason profile discipline: bounded judge work must not run under a generative reason profile. Hosts supply a real environment via Config instead of `NoOpInferenceEnvironment`.

Covers: INF-02.

### `nubble_run_cost_events__event_timestamps` — Record cost and inference events for every harness run (event_timestamps)

Finance asks Nubble whether a harness run burned billable units. He starts the CLI host with the default pass-through family and a mock reason backend, uses the built-in one-shot infer universe (no custom recipe load), runs infer with a short prompt, and verifies completion by reading the event log: an inference event and a cost event with non-zero units — the same signals he would forward to billing. He also checks that those events carry the host clock timestamps he expects. This stage covers the `event_timestamps` scenario.

#### Implementation

CLI universe `cli:infer` via `CliInstrumentor` / `CliInferRunner` emits structured `EventLog` records for inference and cost (`CostAccountant` / `core:cost`, `core:inference`) on the same stream as graph lifecycle events. This is the baseline observability stream for every run — decisions, routing, and tools extend the same log rather than a separate ledger.

Covers: OBS-01.

#### Validation

Harness `user_story` scenarios `event_types.yaml` (environment + infer step + complete event/cost/token expects) and `event_timestamps.yaml` (environment.clock + infer + complete timestamp expects). Cassette `response.json`. Related: `tests/test_events.py`. Live: `MECHA_STORY_BACKEND=live`. Stage id `nubble_run_cost_events__event_timestamps` (scenario `event_timestamps`).

### `fangore_audited_infer_accept` — Expand an audited infer-accept generate and gate spine

Fangore starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`, and works with the `audited_infer_accept` recipe. He wants a generate → freeze criteria → decide → independent QA → deterministic → gate control pattern that a video production host can migrate onto, without shipping Comfy in the library. Soft modality selects text decide/QA kinds; principals for decide and QA differ. Complements `fangore_verify_repair_recipe` (oracle loop) and `fangore_guided_coding_recipe` (which tiles this spine). He walks product steps (instantiate_recipe) and verifies completion from the structured observation expects on this scenario.

#### Implementation

Agentic Recipe catalog id `audited_infer_accept` (`AuditedInferAcceptTemplate` + `append_audited_infer_accept`). Domain `mechaharness.audited_decision` (`STAGES`, `criteria_hash`, `assert_principals_distinct`, `repair_target`). Default node kinds `audited.*`; hosts soft-bind runners (e.g. `host.infer.*`). Migration notes: `docs/inspiration/video-production-audited-infer-migration.md`.

#### Validation

Harness `user_story` scenario `spine.yaml`: environment + instantiate_recipe expects. Unit tests `tests/test_audited_decision.py`.

### `fangore_backend_describe_recipe` — Describe an inference backend through the backend_describe recipe

Fangore starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`, and works with the `backend_describe` recipe. Before Fangore wires a host, he wants a machine-readable description of a configured backend — name, network behavior, auth — without leaving the recipe catalog. He runs backend_describe with the mock backend and gets the same metadata the classic describe command used to print. Complements `fangore_harness_run_recipe`. He walks product steps (run_recipe) and verifies completion from the structured observation expects on this scenario.

#### Implementation

Agentic Recipe catalog id `backend_describe` (`BackendDescribeTemplate`) with a single describe node. `BackendDescribeRunner` calls `InferenceStrategy.describe()` via DI. `CliInstrumentor` verb `run_recipe` calls `recipe_runner.run_backend_describe_recipe`. CLI `describe` / `recipes run backend_describe` share this path. Soft points: backend (required), model, base_url, api_key, describe_kind.

#### Validation

Harness `user_story` scenario `describe_mock.yaml`: environment + graph + steps + complete expects.

### `fangore_bag_checkpoint_persist` — Carry bag evidence across a stepped graph checkpoint

Fangore starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`. He loads a two-node inline graph where the first leaf publishes discovery evidence onto the walk bag (`acc`) and the second leaf requires that register before succeeding. He pauses after the writer (`graph_walk` start / one_step), asserts the bag observation still holds the evidence, then resumes (`step`). The consumer must see the same `acc` values from the checkpoint — not an empty bag — so later inference nodes can trust inter-step continuity.

#### Implementation

`WalkBag.serialize` / `deserialize` on `ExecutionGraph.walk_bag`; `GraphExecutor` hydrates `GraphRunContext.bag` on resume and syncs the bag before every checkpoint save; story-host `graph_walk` runners honor `payload.bag_put` / `payload.bag_require` and surface `bag` on observations.

#### Validation

Suite stage `010_fangore_bag_checkpoint_persist` — start pauses with `bag.acc` populated; step resume completes with the same nested evidence and no `node_error`.

#### Footnotes

1. [Gastronomic guided-development M1 (bag durability)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/gastronomic-guided-development-execution-plan.md) — Checkpoint/resume must carry WalkBag with graph state

### `fangore_bag_context_spec_continuity` — Compile bag evidence into a second inference request

Fangore starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`. He loads an inline graph that seeds a goal plus unrelated bag noise, runs a bag-aware discovery inference that publishes structured hypotheses to `out.discovery`, validates that evidence with a hard compute node into `out.verified`, then pauses before the planning inference. On resume the planner's ContextSpec must compile only the goal, discovery, and verified evidence into the Completer request — not the noise register — and publish `out.plan` from the scripted completion.

#### Implementation

`ContextSpec` / `compile_context_spec` / `publish_response_to_bag` in `context_spec`; bag-aware `CliInferRunner` freezes the walk bag per invocation, records `model_inputs`, and calls Completer; story-host `graph_walk` registers `infer`/`cli:infer` via `CliInferRunner` and surfaces `model_inputs` observations.

#### Validation

Suite stage `030_fangore_bag_context_spec_continuity` — pause before `plan` shows nonempty `bag.out.discovery` and hard-node `out.verified`; continue completes with `model_inputs.plan.includes_verified_discovery=true` and `includes_unrelated_bag_data=false`, plus nonempty `bag.out.plan`. Static mock uses `payload.completion` scripts; live upgrades onto the reason Completer.

#### Footnotes

1. [Gastronomic guided-development M2 (ContextSpec + infer publication)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/gastronomic-guided-development-execution-plan.md) — Second inference must see authorized bag state from the first, not noise

### `fangore_bag_discovery_hard_nodes` — Run P0 discovery hard nodes over a tiny workspace

Fangore starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`. He seeds a calculator workspace and WalkBag hypotheses, then steps deterministic hard nodes — `workspace_manifest`, `file_search`, `source_extract`, `evidence_resolve`, `bag_project`, `bag_validate`, and `coverage_measure` — so verified evidence lands on declared bag paths without partial writes or invented citations.

#### Implementation

`DiscoveryHardNodeRunner` / P0 capabilities in `discovery_hard_nodes`; `graph_walk` registers hard kinds alongside compute / infer / judge. Workspace confinement reuses `WorkspacePaths`.

#### Validation

Suite stage `060_fangore_bag_discovery_hard_nodes` — after the walk, manifest lists two files, search matches `ZeroDivisionError`, `bag.acc.discovery.verified.ok` is false (fabricated path rejected), projected summary omits noise, unrelated bag state is preserved, and coverage is `sufficient`. Typed non-exceptional failures (stale hash, invalid regex, extract rejects, truncation/inconclusive coverage, atomic failed writes) live in `tests/test_discovery_hard_nodes.py`.

#### Footnotes

1. [Gastronomic guided-development M4 (P0 discovery hard nodes)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/gastronomic-guided-development-execution-plan.md) — Deterministic hard nodes publish to declared bag paths only

### `fangore_bag_judge_no_tools` — Judge bag evidence with zero tool definitions

Fangore starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`. He seeds a proposal plus verified evidence (and unrelated noise), then runs a bag-aware `judge` node whose ContextSpec selects only the authorized paths. The judge Completer receives no tool schemas, performs no tool calls, and publishes a typed verdict to `out.judgment`.

#### Implementation

`CliJudgeRunner` compiles `ContextSpec` against a frozen bag snapshot, refuses tool loops, validates typed verdicts, and publishes to the live bag; `graph_walk` registers `judge`/`cli:judge` and surfaces `inference.judge.*`.

#### Validation

Suite stage `050_fangore_bag_judge_no_tools` — continue completes with `inference.judge.tool_call_count=0`, `inference.judge.includes_verified_evidence=true`, and `bag.out.judgment.valid=true`.

1. [Gastronomic guided-development M3 (no-tool judge)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/gastronomic-guided-development-execution-plan.md) — Judges compile bag context but never receive or dispatch tools

### `fangore_bag_snapshot_inspect` — Inspect a frozen bag snapshot while the live bag mutates

Fangore starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`. He seeds verified evidence and a secret noise register, runs a prior bag-aware inference that publishes a note, then an agent inference whose ContextSpec plus `inspection` tools call `inspect_bag` twice around a live-bag mutation, attempt an unauthorized path, and inspect the prior response. The two authorized bag reads must match the frozen snapshot, the forbidden path must be denied, and tool results must appear in the inference transcript.

#### Implementation

`SnapshotInspectionToolkit` in `bag_inspect`; bag-aware `CliInferRunner` inspection tool loop bound to one frozen snapshot; prior responses recorded for `inspect_prior_response`; `graph_walk` surfaces `inference.*` observations.

#### Validation

Suite stage `040_fangore_bag_snapshot_inspect` — after continue, `inference.agent.inspection_snapshot_stable`, `unauthorized_inspection_denied`, and `tool_results_in_transcript` are true.

#### Footnotes

1. [Gastronomic guided-development M3 (snapshot inspection)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/gastronomic-guided-development-execution-plan.md) — Inspection tools read the invocation snapshot, not live bag mutations

### `fangore_bag_subgraph_bindings` — Map parent bag into a subgraph and publish declared outputs only

Fangore starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`. He loads a parent graph that seeds `acc.discovery`, nests a subgraph with `bag_inputs` / `bag_outputs`, and continues to completion. The child must see a deep-copied projection of discovery on `in`, and only the declared `out` mapping may appear on the parent bag afterward — child mutations of nested input values must not rewrite the parent's `acc.discovery`.

#### Implementation

### `fangore_graph_executor` — Run a local plan through an authorized graph executor

Fangore starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`. Fangore ships a host app with a produce → repair → consume plan. After linkage succeeds, the library must walk ready steps, refuse execution without an execute grant, retry transient failures, escalate when retries are exhausted, emit start and end telemetry, and finish the downstream consume step only after upstream success. Checkpointed plans from `fangore_local_plan_resume` stay durable; preflight failures are covered by `fangore_graph_linkage_preflight`. See inspiration requirements for authorized graph execution[^insp-executor].

#### Implementation

`GraphExecutor` in `mechaharness.graph_executor` is a pyiv injectable: constructor takes `EventLog`, `AccessControl`, `GraphNodeRunnerRegistry`, `GraphFailurePolicy`, `GraphEscalation`, and `LinkageResolver`. Hosts register node runners by open `kind` string via `MechaHarnessConfig.get_node_runner_registry()`, override failure/escalation/linkage hooks, and grant `core:graph.execute` / `core:graph.escalate`. The executor emits `core:graph_start` / `core:graph_end` plus per-node events. `CliInstrumentor` verb `graph_executor_run` exercises the path.

Acceptance walks the registered CLI verb (TestHarnessCliConfig promotes remaining story probes when no src product verb exists yet).

#### Validation

Harness `user_story` walks the promoted product/test verb (no `probe:` wrapper); hard expects on declared observation keys.

#### Footnotes

[^loop-vs-graph-executor]: [Loop vs graph engineering](https://medium.com/@neuraldev/loop-engineering-vs-graph-engineering-the-architecture-shift-quietly-reshaping-ai-agents-c83488435d23) — Executor advances durable plans hosts define
[^insp-executor]: [Inspiration requirements (graph execution)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/dev-blog-inspiration.md) — Reqs 2 and 12 — linkage then execute; durable checkpoints

The library must refuse those plans before any runner work starts, naming the missing edge so operators can fix wiring instead of debugging a mid-run crash. `DefaultLinkageResolver` preflight; `CliInstrumentor` verb `graph_linkage_preflight`.

Each declares `SoftPoint`s; `GraphTemplate.instantiate` builds via `build` then stamps `template_name`, `template_version`, `template_status`, and optional `source_workflow_ref`. Demoted templates refuse instantiate. Bound via `MechaHarnessConfig.get_graph_template_registry()`.

### `fangore_guided_coding_recipe__helper_run_python` — Guide local coding via the guided_coding Agentic Recipe (helper_run_python)

Fangore starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`, loads the `guided_coding` durable graph (controller `story`, store `memory`). He wants Cursor to answer only short engineering direction while a project-local MechaHarness process classifies oneshot vs todo list and does the token-heavy file edits under pre/item/post acceptance. Start yields `advice_requested` from soft point `external_guidance`; he answers `minimal` in a later call and the run completes. In a workspace-backed walk he has the agent write a small helper module, confirms the file on disk, and runs Python against it to check stdout. Git inspect and mocked pull-request handoffs are owned by `fangore_coding_git_inspect` and `fangore_coding_git_open_pr`. Complements `fangore_instruction_todo_plan`, `fangore_insp_graph_guidance_yield`, and `fangore_conversational_tool_loop`. He walks product steps (start, answer, workspace_read, run_python) and verifies completion from the structured observation expects on each scenario. This stage covers the `helper_run_python` scenario.

#### Implementation

Agentic Recipe catalog id `guided_coding` (`GuidedCodingTemplate`) tiles `instruction_todo_plan` and `audited_infer_accept` under `plan_tile` / `audit_tile` with soft point `external_guidance` (`kind=guidance`). MCP `MECHA_MCP_HOST=project_coding` binds `ProjectCodingConfig` (workspace coding tools + `GeneratorLocalWork` / `ProjectCodingLocalWork` burst after guidance, including `request_guidance` restart for plan refinement). Injectable `CodingGit` (default `LocalProcessCodingGit`; story/CI often `RecordingPullRequestCodingGit`) backs optional git/PR tools — see `fangore_coding_git_inspect` / `fangore_coding_git_open_pr`. Story hosts bind `environment.local_work: project_coding` with a temp workspace and optional `coding_write` stub. `ProjectCodingLocalWork` records `written_files` / `workspace_root` on the completed yield. Product verbs `workspace_read` and `run_python` put file text and stdout/stderr/exit_code into the step observation bag. `DurableGraphGenerator._advance` invokes the injectable local-work hook when the guidance queue is empty.

#### Validation

Harness `user_story` scenarios `session.yaml` (NoOp guidance smoke) and `helper_run_python.yaml` (project_coding workspace write + workspace_read + run_python expects). Both scenarios pin generator counters (`guidance_yields` / `resumes` / `local_steps`) and `tapped_event_types` / `event_types` so unexpected durable or coding-graph executions fail hard. Unit tests `tests/test_project_coding.py` (including git tool confinement / unsafe-ref rejection), `tests/test_guided_coding_recipe.py`, and `tests/test_cli_workspace_verbs.py` cover tools confinement, plan/audit tile topology, offline local-work file write, and workspace verbs. Stage id `fangore_guided_coding_recipe__helper_run_python` (scenario `helper_run_python`).

Module doctests document the blessed host path.

Acceptance walks the registered CLI verb (TestHarnessCliConfig promotes remaining story probes when no src product verb exists yet).

### `fangore_insp_decision_conflict_checkpoint__cleared_at_c` — Checkpoint after conflict-free decisions without revisiting cleared cycles (cleared_at_c)

Fangore starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`. After a decision is settled, the nodes it still conflicts with are revisited, and nodes already visited are not revisited so a circular conflict cannot loop forever. A checkpoint is taken only when the decision has no remaining conflicts; a conflict blocked only by the visited set is reported instead of silently saved. The conflicts themselves are still the write-scope conflicts the product already detects (`fangore_tdr_crash_after_accept_before_record`, `fangore_decision_plane_policy`); this adds the revisit-and-checkpoint rule on top. Tracks MH-SR-08[^insp-sr-08]. This stage covers the `cleared_at_c` scenario.

#### Implementation

`neighbor_revisit` / `neighbors_from_write_conflicts`. `CliInstrumentor` verb `decision_conflict_neighbor_revisit`.

Acceptance walks the registered CLI verb (TestHarnessCliConfig promotes remaining story probes when no src product verb exists yet).

#### Validation

Harness `user_story` walks the promoted product/test verb (no `probe:` wrapper); hard expects on declared observation keys. Stage id `fangore_insp_decision_conflict_checkpoint__cleared_at_c` (scenario `cleared_at_c`).

### `fangore_insp_evolution_ownership_split` — Keep recipe validation in the library and evolution campaigns in the host

Fangore starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`. MechaHarness validates, executes, versions, and safety-gates recipes; the host (for example an AI assistant project) owns which workloads to run, how much to spend, and whether a candidate should be promoted. Two named hooks carry that split: one for evolution campaigns and one for promotion policy. Both default to doing nothing, a host can replace either, a host veto stops a promotion even when every test passed, and the library's final-test gate still applies when the host has no opinion (`taloneth_insp_recipe_final_test_gate`). He walks product steps (recipe_plan) and verifies completion from the structured observation expects on this scenario. [^insp-sr-09]

#### Implementation

`MechaHarnessConfig.get_recipe_promotion_policy()` (`RecipePromotionPolicy`, default `NoopRecipePromotionPolicy`) and `get_evolution_campaign_hooks()` (`EvolutionCampaignHooks`, default `NoopEvolutionCampaignHooks`) are registered in `configure()` as injectables, not `Settings`. `promote_recipe()` in `recipe_promotion_policy.py` lets the host policy decide, then the registry applies `promote_with_final_test`; when given the Config-bound hooks it calls `EvolutionCampaignHooks.on_promotion` after (and only after) a successful pointer move. Registry validation, evolvable allowlists, and the final-test gate stay in the library.

#### Validation

Harness `user_story` scenario `evolution_ownership_split.yaml`: environment + graph + steps + complete expects.

#### Footnotes

[^insp-sr-09]: [Self-revising recipe evolution (MH-SR-09)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/self-revising-recipe-evolution.md) — AI assistant host versus MechaHarness ownership for evolution

### `fangore_insp_recipe_lineage_promote` — Attach lineage and test results when promoting a recipe version

Fangore starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`. New recipe versions are immutable artifacts with provenance, lineage, test results, and a reversible promotion pointer. He walks product steps (recipe_plan) and verifies completion from the structured observation expects on this scenario. [^insp-sr-05]

#### Implementation

`GraphTemplateRegistry.add_version(template, parent_version=...)` records the lineage DAG and refuses to replace a stored name+version; `attach_evaluation` / `evaluations` hang eval results on a version; `promote` and `rollback` move a reversible pointer; `merge` carries versions, lineage, evaluations, and pointer. Held-out release gates (MH-SR-07) and the evolution loop (MH-SR-06) remain separate stories.

#### Validation

Harness `user_story` scenario `recipe_registry_versions.yaml`: environment + graph + steps + complete expects.

### `fangore_insp_recipe_port_search` — Search compatible recipe compositions by typed ports

Fangore starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`. Candidate compositions are found by searching only the registered recipes for ones whose declared inputs and outputs fit what is needed. The answer is a list of recipe names; nothing is generated, so no new executable code can enter the production path. A recipe that declares no ports is never suggested, and a type mismatch rules a recipe out. He walks product steps (recipe_plan) and verifies completion from the structured observation expects on this scenario. [^insp-sr-04] Related: `fangore_insp_isolation_io`.

#### Implementation

`search_compatible_recipes(registry, required_inputs, required_outputs)` in `recipe_port_search.py` compares each active recipe's `GraphTemplate.io_contract` (`TemplateIOContract` from `isolation_contract.py`) with the requested ports (type equality, `any` as a wildcard) and returns sorted catalog ids only. `io_contract` is declared on `safety_eval`, `independent_review`, `produce_critique_refine`, `verify_repair`, and `fan_out_aggregate`; other recipes are skipped until they declare ports.

#### Validation

Harness `user_story` scenario `recipe_port_search.yaml`: environment + graph + steps + complete expects.

#### Footnotes

[^insp-sr-04]: [Self-revising recipe evolution (MH-SR-04)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/self-revising-recipe-evolution.md) — Typed-port composition search

### `fangore_insp_recipe_version_pointer` — Promote and roll back recipes via an immutable version pointer

Fangore starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`. Recipe execution policies are versioned, testable, replaceable artifacts with a reversible promotion pointer — not only class version fields and demotion stamps. Incubation stamps exist in `fangore_insp_template_incubation`; lineage and evaluation attachments are in `fangore_insp_recipe_lineage_promote`. Tracks MH-SR-01. He walks product steps (recipe_plan) and verifies completion from the structured observation expects on this scenario. [^insp-sr-01]

#### Implementation

`GraphTemplateRegistry` stores every version of a catalog id (here `verify_repair`): `add_version` registers an immutable inactive candidate, `promote(name, version)` moves the active pointer, `rollback(name)` restores the previous target, and `get(name, version=...)` reads any stored version. `register` keeps legacy activate-by-name semantics. Eval results and promotion policy stay host-owned.

#### Validation

Harness `user_story` scenario `recipe_registry_versions.yaml`: environment + graph + steps + complete expects.

#### Footnotes

[^insp-sr-01]: [Self-revising recipe evolution (MH-SR-01)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/self-revising-recipe-evolution.md) — Versioned replaceable recipe artifacts

`DefaultLinkageResolver` stop-contract edge; `CliInstrumentor` verb `graph_linkage_preflight`.

Harness `user_story` drives product verb(s) with environment `pass_through`/`mock`; hard expects on declared observation keys.

`attribute_with_repair_target` / `select_rollback_target`; `CliInstrumentor` verb `targeted_rollback_select`.

Fangore starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`, and works with the `fan_out_aggregate` recipe. Reusable Agentic Recipes expose soft points and stamp provenance onto concrete graphs. Demoted templates that proved application-specific refuse instantiate. Accepts inspiration requirement 19. He walks product steps (instantiate_recipe, recipe_plan) and verifies completion from the structured observation expects on this scenario. `GraphTemplate` is the substrate for Agentic Recipes. `SoftPoint`, `GraphTemplate.stamp`, `status` active/deprecated/demoted, and optional `source_workflow_ref` support incubation. This story stamps and demotes via the `fan_out_aggregate` catalog entry.

#### Validation

Harness `user_story` scenario `graph_template_soft_points.yaml`: environment + graph + steps + complete expects.

### `fangore_instruction_todo_plan__conflict_list_refinement` — Execute oneshot or todo-list instructions via instruction_todo_plan (conflict_list_refinement)

Fangore starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`, loads the `instruction_todo_plan` durable graph (controller `story`, store `memory`). He wants the local agent to judge whether a task is a oneshot or an ordered list, refine conflicts before work, verify pre-list and per-item acceptance, then check post-list acceptance so later todos have not undone earlier ones. With plan_classify local work he can ask for a oneshot helper from a goal, follow a numbered instruction list, resolve conflicting todos via list refinement, or force list mode explicitly. A separate session schedules scope refinement guidance when he answers oneshot without classify. Complements `fangore_guided_coding_recipe` (which tiles this recipe as `plan_tile`). He walks product steps (start, answer) and verifies completion from the structured observation expects on each scenario. This stage covers the `conflict_list_refinement` scenario.

#### Implementation

Agentic Recipe catalog id `instruction_todo_plan` (`InstructionTodoPlanTemplate`) with stages classify → refine_plan → pre_accept → work_item* → item_accept → post_accept → complete. Domain `mechaharness.instruction_plan` builds the plan; `PlanClassifyLocalWork` runs classify/refine without a coding tool loop for offline stories (`environment.local_work: plan_classify`). Optional soft points `scope_refinement` / `list_refinement` (`kind=guidance`, not required) are requested via local-work `request_guidance` (or scheduled in inputs.guidance for offline smoke). `DurableGraphGenerator._advance` enqueues those asks, yields `advice_requested`, and restarts local work after resume with `guidance_history`. Step observations lift allowlisted yield payload fields (`context_version`, `mode`, `plan`) for path expects.

#### Validation

Harness `user_story` scenarios `session.yaml` (scheduled scope_refinement), `oneshot_from_goal.yaml`, `numbered_list.yaml`, `conflict_list_refinement.yaml`, `explicit_list_mode.yaml`. Unit tests `tests/test_instruction_todo_plan.py` and `tests/test_instruction_plan_integration.py` (`classify_mode`) cover topology and pure classifier edges. Stage id `fangore_instruction_todo_plan__conflict_list_refinement` (scenario `conflict_list_refinement`).

### `fangore_local_plan_resume` — Resume a durable local plan after a crash

Fangore starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`. A local plan's require_file node fails when `/work/input.txt` is missing on the virtual filesystem. He observes that failure, seeds the file into MemoryFilesystem, and resumes the same checkpointed `run_id` (held on walk-bag `ctx`) so the node succeeds. Checkpoints — not chat — carry the plan across the gap. Incompatible harness fingerprints remain covered by `fangore_insp_durable_resume`. See inspiration requirements for durable long-running work[^insp-resume].

#### Implementation

`LocalPlanResumeVerb` (`local_plan_resume`) in `cli_policy_verbs`: shared `MemoryFilesystem` + `GraphExecutor` checkpoint store; fail on missing path; seed; re-arm failed node; `resume=True` with the same `run_id` on walk-bag `ctx`. Fan-in / merge / precondition helpers stay available as library units; fingerprint refuse is `fangore_insp_durable_resume`.

#### Validation

Harness `user_story` walks `local_plan_resume`; expects first_status=failed (missing_file), resume_status=ok, file_content, and stable run_id.

#### Footnotes

[^loop-vs-graph]: [Loop vs graph engineering](https://medium.com/@neuraldev/loop-engineering-vs-graph-engineering-the-architecture-shift-quietly-reshaping-ai-agents-c83488435d23) — Explicit control flow; MechaHarness extends into execution graphs
[^insp-resume]: [Inspiration requirements (durable resume)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/dev-blog-inspiration.md) — Req 12 — resumable external state; incompatible fingerprint refuse

### `fangore_node_components` — Query node components inside each graph node for pre-layout

Fangore starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`, and works with the `conversational_tool_loop` recipe. Before a run starts, Fangore’s console must place interior pieces inside each plan step — soft bindings, stop bounds, and nested child handles — so the camera can zoom into a node without inventing a parallel structure graph. Those pieces are node components of a parent graph node, not free-floating world nodes. Complements `fangore_insp_dynamic_subgraph` and `fangore_traversal_contract`. He walks product steps (instantiate_recipe) and verifies completion from the structured observation expects on this scenario. [^ai-asst-nc-req]

#### Implementation

`mechaharness.node_component.node_components_for` derives `NodeComponent` rows from an `ExecutionGraph` plus optional template soft points and tool names. Kinds are limited to the closed catalog in `docs/reference/node-components.md` (events, soft points, child_graph, stop_contract, effect_state, budget_level). Every component requires `parent_node_id`. Soft points on Agentic Recipes appear as `soft_point` components.

#### Validation

Harness `user_story` scenario `node_components.yaml`: environment + graph + steps + complete expects.

#### Footnotes

[^ai-asst-nc-req]: [Dynamic tool graph and node components](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/requirements/dynamic-tool-graph.md) — Vocabulary and kind rule

Parent exposes a `child_graph` node component via `node_components_for`.

Harness `user_story` scenario `recipe_as_tool.yaml`: environment + graph + steps + complete expects.

[^ai-asst-hf08]: [AI assistant host-friction requirements map](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/ai-assistant-host-friction-requirements-map.md) — HF-08 recipe-as-tool

### `fangore_refund_verdict` — Keep billing authority in product rules, not the model

Fangore starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`. A customer was charged twice. Only the billing team may own the ticket. The model may suggest a team, but product policy allows only when the route signal is billing — and a high quality score alone must not override missing completion evidence. He walks product steps (judge_route) and verifies completion from the structured observation expects on this scenario. Related: `fangore_decision_surface_reject`.

#### Implementation

Provider-neutral judge types (`Choice`/`Score`/`Noul` questions and signals) plus `JudgementPolicy` / `decide()` apply configured thresholds. `CliInstrumentor` verb `judge_route` runs judge+decide. System One maps vendor wire via `SystemOneJudgeProvider`.

Covers: POL-02, JDG-01, JDG-02, JDG-04, VER-02.

#### Validation

Harness `user_story` scenario `billing_allow.yaml`: environment + graph + steps + complete expects. Live (`MECHA_STORY_BACKEND=live` + `MECHA_JUDGE_*`): same scenario via `SystemOneJudgeProvider` (cassette-exact token softens; behavioral expects hard).

1. [Jev decisions in a Pi harness](https://academy.dair.ai/resources/jev-decisions-in-a-pi-sdk-harness) — Routing, gating, batched questions, thresholds

### `fangore_tdr_crash_after_accept_before_record` — Resume after remote accept before the plan records the result

Fangore starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`. He dispatches a remote coding job on a durable plan; the MechaHarness process dies after the remote system accepts but before acceptance is recorded. After restart he opens the same durable store, resumes the plan, and verifies the remote job is submitted exactly once with the expected effect state for this crash window. Sibling windows: `fangore_tdr_crash_before_intent`, `fangore_tdr_crash_after_intent_before_call`, `fangore_tdr_crash_after_accept_before_record`, `fangore_tdr_crash_after_accept_recorded`, `fangore_tdr_crash_after_reduce_before_checkpoint`, and `fangore_tdr_crash_after_final_commit`. Complements `fangore_insp_durable_resume` fingerprint refusal. Tracks transactional durable resume[^tdr-req] and MH-PA-05[^insp-pa-05]. He walks product steps (`transactional_resume`) and verifies completion from the structured observation expects on this scenario.

#### Implementation

`SqliteCheckpointStore` + `host_graph_executor` with `ArmedCrashProbe` for coding_job effects. Product CLI verb `transactional_resume` (`mechaharness.cli_transactional_resume`). Unit matrix: `tests/fixtures/transactional_durable_resume/*.json`.

#### Validation

Harness `user_story` scenario `crash_after_accept_before_record.yaml` drives product verb `transactional_resume` with `crash_location: after_accept_before_record`; hard expects on declared observation keys.

### `fangore_tdr_crash_before_intent` — Resume after crash before the job intent is recorded

Fangore starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`. He dispatches a remote coding job on a durable plan; the MechaHarness process dies before the job intent is recorded. After restart he opens the same durable store, resumes the plan, and verifies the remote job is submitted exactly once with the expected effect state for this crash window. Sibling windows: `fangore_tdr_crash_before_intent`, `fangore_tdr_crash_after_intent_before_call`, `fangore_tdr_crash_after_accept_before_record`, `fangore_tdr_crash_after_accept_recorded`, `fangore_tdr_crash_after_reduce_before_checkpoint`, and `fangore_tdr_crash_after_final_commit`. Complements `fangore_insp_durable_resume` fingerprint refusal. Tracks transactional durable resume[^tdr-req] and MH-PA-05[^insp-pa-05]. He walks product steps (`transactional_resume`) and verifies completion from the structured observation expects on this scenario.

#### Implementation

`SqliteCheckpointStore` + `host_graph_executor` with `ArmedCrashProbe` for coding_job effects. Product CLI verb `transactional_resume` (`mechaharness.cli_transactional_resume`). Unit matrix: `tests/fixtures/transactional_durable_resume/*.json`.

#### Validation

Harness `user_story` scenario `crash_before_intent.yaml` drives product verb `transactional_resume` with `crash_location: before_intent`; hard expects on declared observation keys.

## Taloneth's stories

### `taloneth_atk_research_reject` — Reject research candidates that fail verified success

Taloneth starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`. A cheap backend fails verified success against a frozen baseline. Research must reject it, keep negative results, and only promote noninferior survivors. Candidates cannot rewrite the evaluator. Related: `taloneth_validator_qualification`. Generic research loop for self-revising MH-SR-06; recipe-from-traces: `taloneth_insp_recipe_evolution_loop`[^insp-sr-06-research].

#### Implementation

`ResearchLab` / `EvalProtocol` run bounded research: inspect → hypothesis → isolated experiment → ATK-style search → frozen evaluation protocol → promote/rollback. Production evaluators stay protected.

Covers: EXP-01, EXP-02, EXP-03, EXP-04.

#### Validation

Harness `user_story` drives product verb(s) with environment `pass_through`/`mock`; hard expects on declared observation keys.

### `taloneth_insp_correction_spec_debt` — Capture corrections as reviewed specification debt before policy change

Taloneth starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`. When a person corrects the agent, the correction is recorded as outstanding specification debt: the correction text, the scenarios that failed, and a link to the rule-promotion record it may harden into. The record stays flagged for human review until someone accepts it, and the host (not the library) generates the regression test and attaches it. Soft-to-hard promotion with provenance exists in `taloneth_insp_rule_promotion`. Tracks MH-PA-07[^insp-pa-07].

#### Implementation

`SpecificationDebtRecord`, `SpecificationDebtLedger`, and `capture_correction()` in `specification_debt.py` hold the correction, `failing_scenario_refs`, `promotion_record_id` (from `PromotionRecord.record_id`), `review_required`, and a host-filled `generated_test_ref`; `link_test()` and `approve()` move status `open` → `test_linked` → `closed`. The library owns only the ledger schema; test generation stays with the host.

Acceptance walks the registered CLI verb (TestHarnessCliConfig promotes remaining story probes when no src product verb exists yet).

#### Validation

Harness `user_story` walks the promoted product/test verb (no `probe:` wrapper); hard expects on declared observation keys.

#### Footnotes

[^insp-pa-07]: [Personal agent reliability (MH-PA-07)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/personal-agent-reliability-inspiration.md) — Correction-to-test feedback

### `taloneth_insp_recipe_evolution_loop` — Evolve recipe candidates from traces under registry and safety gates

Taloneth starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`. A host can summarize past traces into suggestions, and the library turns them into a short list of candidate recipe settings that stay inside the catalog and inside the settings marked safe to tune. Anything that names an unknown recipe, an unknown or fixed setting, or a setting the host did not allow is reported as rejected rather than quietly dropped. Candidates are then chosen by an explicit scoring policy that respects its gates and a baseline. They walk product steps (recipe_plan) and verify completion from the structured observation expects on this scenario. [^insp-sr-06] Related: `taloneth_insp_recipe_final_test_gate`.

#### Implementation

`recipe_evolution.py`: `RecipeTraceSummary` / `SoftBindingSuggestion` in, `propose_candidates()` out as `RecipeCandidate` soft-binding dicts validated by `validate_candidate()` against `GraphTemplateRegistry` names, `GraphTemplate.evolvable_soft_point_names()`, and an optional host allowlist; `select_candidate()` picks over `ScoredCandidate` results built from `ObjectivePolicy` / `aggregate_objective` with a deterministic tie-break. Pure structure for hosts such as an AI assistant project; evaluation reuses `ResearchLab` and the registry final-test gate.

#### Validation

Harness `user_story` scenario `recipe_evolution_candidates.yaml`: environment + graph + steps + complete expects.

#### Footnotes

[^insp-sr-06]: [Self-revising recipe evolution (MH-SR-06)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/self-revising-recipe-evolution.md) — Candidate evolution loop

### `taloneth_insp_recipe_final_test_gate` — Require an untouched final test set before recipe promotion

Taloneth starts the CLI host with family `pass_through` and backend `mock`. A leading candidate must pass a separate untouched final test before it can be released, and that test must not be used as a tuning signal. Promotion is refused when no final-test result is supplied, when the result did not come from a held-out evaluator, or when it failed; only a passing held-out result opens the gate. The same rule guards both the research workflow and the recipe catalog's active pointer. They walk product steps (recipe_plan) and verify completion from the structured observation expects on this scenario. [^insp-sr-07] Related: `taloneth_insp_evaluator_compose`.

#### Implementation

`require_held_out_final_test()` and `FinalTestGateError` in `evaluator.py`; `ResearchLab.promote(candidate, final_test=...)` enforces it whenever `EvalProtocol.held_out_protected` (the default); `GraphTemplateRegistry.promote_with_final_test()` applies it before moving the active pointer and attaches the held-out result as an evaluation. Plain `GraphTemplateRegistry.promote()` stays an ungated pointer move for hosts that run their own gate.

#### Validation

Harness `user_story` scenario `recipe_final_test_gate.yaml`: environment + graph + steps + complete expects.

#### Footnotes

[^insp-sr-07]: [Self-revising recipe evolution (MH-SR-07)](https://github.com/rl337/mechaharness/blob/main/docs/inspiration/self-revising-recipe-evolution.md) — Held-out final-test release gate
